summary: A11y/motion audit: unguarded cursor rAF loop, keyboard/SR gaps in radar+terminal+VIP panel, light-theme accent text fails WCAG AA contrast, v27 particle-fx never actually shipped.
result_text:
TRACK 4 — Accessibility & Motion/Performance UX Audit
Repo HEAD at audit time: 04f3c365 (main). Scope: assets/css/style.css, reduced-motion/focus-visible logic, and all canvas/rAF surfaces. Verified against live repo, not assumed from tracker prose.

---

[HIGH] Custom cursor rAF loop has no reduced-motion or visibilitychange guard
File: assets/js/modules/core.js:591-611 (initCursor / tick())
Only gate is `matchMedia('(pointer: fine)')`. The `tick()` function calls `requestAnimationFrame(tick)` unconditionally and recurses forever — no `prefers-reduced-motion` check, no Page Visibility API pause. CSS (style.css:1617-1636) does hide `.cursor` under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (`display: none !important`), so v44's "reduced-motion cursor reset" only patched the visual layer — the JS loop keeps computing and writing `style.left/top` on invisible elements indefinitely, in every tab state. This breaks the pattern the codebase otherwise follows consistently: cursor-trail (ui.js:456), scroll-parallax (haptics.js:99-100), tour (tour.js:70), and the two index.html background canvases (SignalWaveBackground/PCBTraces, index.html:1520-1524) all check `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` before starting, and the two background canvases additionally gate on `visibilitychange`/`IntersectionObserver` (index.html:1305-1312). initCursor is the one rAF loop that inherited neither.
Fix: add `if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) return;` at top of initCursor, and a `document.hidden` / visibilitychange check inside tick() to stop the loop when the tab is backgrounded.

[HIGH] Light-theme --accent fails WCAG AA text contrast (1.4.3) — 62 usages of `color: var(--accent)` in style.css
Measured (WCAG relative-luminance formula): light-mode `--accent` (#d97706) on `--bg` (#faf8f4) = 3.00:1; on `--bg2`/white = 3.19:1. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal-size text (only 3:1 for large text ≥24px/19px-bold, or for non-text UI components per 1.4.11). Confirmed real small-text instances using this exact failing pair:
  - style.css:652 `.nav-logo span` (brand accent letter)
  - style.css:680 `.nav-links a:hover, .nav-links a.active` — 0.78rem (~12.5px) uppercase nav text, actively fails
  - style.css:696 `.nav-cta` — 0.78rem mono text on transparent/light bg
  62 total `color: var(--accent)` declarations exist site-wide (grep count); the above three are confirmed small-text/light-mode-affecting via direct read, the remainder were not individually re-verified this pass and should be spot-checked before assuming pass/fail per-instance.
Dark-mode is fine: dark `--accent` (#d4a85a) on dark `--bg` = 8.77:1, `--bg3` = 7.66:1 — both comfortably pass.
Note: this same --accent color is also used for the global `:focus-visible` ring (style.css:1599-1602). That usage is NOT broken — non-text UI component contrast (WCAG 1.4.11) only requires 3:1, and 3.00-3.19:1 clears that bar (barely). Only the *text* usages fail; do not "fix" this by changing the focus-ring color without separately handling the text-color instances, and don't assume the focus ring needs the same fix as the text does.
Fix: darken light-mode `--accent` for text contexts (a ~15-20% luminance reduction gets to ~4.5:1), or introduce a separate `--accent-text` token distinct from the UI/border/focus-ring `--accent` token.

[MEDIUM] Skill radar interactive controls (about.html) are mouse/pointer-only, canvas has no accessible name
Files: about.html:1000 (canvas), assets/js/modules/ui.js:687-708 (.domain-item wiring)
`.domain-item` elements are plain `<div>`s (about.html:1002 onward) with only `mouseenter` (ui.js:693) and `click` (ui.js:702) listeners — no `tabindex`, no `role="button"`, no `keydown`/Enter-Space handler. Keyboard-only users cannot change which radar axis is highlighted at all. `<canvas id="skillRadarCanvas">` (about.html:1000) has no `aria-label`, `role="img"`, or `aria-hidden` — screen readers get nothing from it (the underlying data is duplicated as visible text in the adjacent `.domain-desc`/`.domain-tech-tags` markup, so the fix is to mark the canvas `aria-hidden="true"` rather than trying to describe a live chart).
Fix: give each `.domain-item` `tabindex="0" role="button"` + a keydown handler for Enter/Space mirroring the click handler; add `aria-hidden="true"` to the canvas.
Correction to task framing: this is NOT a continuous rAF/canvas animation — `renderRadar()` (ui.js:622) is called once on load and again only on discrete hover/click events, no animation loop exists, so no reduced-motion/visibilitychange guard is applicable or missing here — the finding is purely keyboard/SR access, not motion.

[MEDIUM] Cert lightbox declares aria-modal="true" without an actual focus trap
Files: achievements.html:730 (`<div id="cert-lightbox" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Certificate viewer">`), assets/js/modules/ui.js:294-361 (initLightbox)
Good: focus moves to `lbClose` on open (ui.js:330), returns to the triggering element on close (ui.js:344, via `lastFocus`), Escape closes it (ui.js:357-359). Missing: no Tab-key containment — nothing in initLightbox intercepts Tab/Shift+Tab to keep focus cycling within the dialog's own controls (close/download/open/verify). A sighted keyboard user can Tab straight through the dialog buttons out to the page content underneath, which contradicts the `aria-modal="true"` contract and the ARIA APG dialog pattern.
Fix: add a Tab keydown handler in the dialog's keydown listener that wraps focus between the first and last focusable element inside `#cert-lightbox` while `.open`.

[MEDIUM] Terminal output region has no aria-live/role="log" — command results are silent to screen readers
Files: index.html:1058 (`.terminal-body`), assets/js/modules/terminal.js:232-238 (appendOutput)
The input is correctly labeled (`aria-label="Terminal command input"`, index.html:1067) and the 9 quick-command buttons are real `<button>` elements with visible text (keyboard-accessible, fine). But `appendOutput()` injects new `.term-line` divs into `.terminal-body` via `innerHTML` with no `aria-live` region and no `role="log"` on the container — a screen-reader user who types a command gets no announcement of its output at all, only silence, since the DOM mutation isn't in a live region.
Fix: add `role="log" aria-live="polite"` to `.terminal-body` (index.html:1058).

[LOW] Master Control Panel (VIP allowlist manager) popup has no ARIA dialog semantics or focus management
File: assets/js/modules/access.js:745-820 (renderMasterControlPanel)
`#masterCardPopup` is toggled via plain `classList.toggle('open')` (access.js:791) — no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-expanded` on `#masterToggleBtn` reflecting open state, no `aria-haspopup`, and focus is never moved into the popup on open or restored to the toggle button on close (Escape just removes the `.open` class, access.js:797-799). Each per-email "remove" button (access.js:834) has only a `title="Remove VIP Access"` attribute with `✕` as its text content — per the accname computation order, visible text content wins over `title` for the accessible name, so every remove button across a multi-email list gets the identical ambiguous accessible name "✕" with no indication of which email it removes.
Severity kept LOW rather than MEDIUM because this entire panel is gated behind Tier 2 (Master-only) access — reachable only by the site owner's own authenticated session, not by any public visitor — so real-world exposure is effectively zero, but it's still a genuine defect if flagged in scope.
Fix (if prioritized): add `role="dialog" aria-label="Master Control Panel"` to the popup, `aria-expanded` toggling on the trigger button, and `aria-label="Remove ${email} from VIP allowlist"` on each remove button.

[HIGH — documentation/reality mismatch, not a code bug per se] Tracker's v27 "about-photo-fx" ambient particle effect does not exist anywhere in the repo
Files checked: about.html, assets/js/script.js, assets/js/modules/*.js, assets/css/style.css — across full git history (`git log -S"about-photo-fx" --all`, 866 commits) with zero hits in any of those files at any commit.
dev-logs/PortfolioWebsite_TRACKER.md's v27 entry (lines ~69-76) describes, in detail, a `<canvas id="about-photo-fx">` inserted into about.html, a CSS positioning rule, and a JS IIFE with a `prefers-reduced-motion` check + Page Visibility gating — and explicitly notes at the end of that same entry: "Not committed/pushed from this side — code delivered inline in-conversation... sync.ps1... wasn't run this session." That commit evidently never happened. The only surviving trace anywhere in the codebase is a dangling selector in a `@media print` hide-list: `assets/css/style.css:3348` (`.about-photo-fx,` — one of several selectors set to `display: none !important` for print; harmless since the element doesn't exist, but dead/orphaned CSS).
This directly affects this track's original task framing, which listed "about-photo-fx particle burst" as one of the canvas features to check for a reduced-motion/visibilitychange guard — there is nothing to check; the feature is vapor. Flag to the tracker owner: either implement it for real (the IIFE text is fully specified in the v27 tracker entry and could be applied verbatim) or strike the entry/claim from the tracker so future audits don't chase a non-existent file.

[CLARIFICATION — corrects task framing, not a bug] "Matrix rain" terminal command is not a canvas/rAF animation
File: assets/js/modules/terminal.js:221-229 (COMMANDS.matrix)
Generates 6 lines of random 0/1 characters once and appends them as static HTML text to the terminal output (same appendOutput() path as any other command result) — no canvas, no requestAnimationFrame, no continuous motion. No reduced-motion guard is needed or missing here.

---

Summary of actual rAF/canvas animation-guard inventory (the real surface for the "does every rAF/canvas feature since v27 have a guard" question):
  - SignalWaveBackground (index.html) — guarded correctly (matchMedia gate before construction + visibilitychange + IntersectionObserver pause/resume).
  - PCBTraces (index.html) — guarded correctly, same pattern.
  - Cursor-trail particles (ui.js:456) — guarded correctly (reduced-motion + touch check).
  - Custom cursor ring/dot (core.js:591) — NOT guarded (see HIGH finding above). This is the one regression/gap.
  - Skill radar, terminal matrix — not actually animations, no guard applicable (see clarifications).
  - about-photo-fx — doesn't exist in the repo (see finding above).

Not covered this pass (ran out of scope budget): full manual contrast sweep of all 62 --accent text usages beyond the 3 confirmed instances; dark-mode focus-visible contrast on --bg3 surfaces; mobile drawer/hamburger keyboard trap check.
